title: Authentication Flow
summary: Put it all together: login, store a token, attach it, and guard routes.
heading: Authentication Flow

blocks.text: Real auth combines four things you've already learned: a service holds the token, the user logs in, an interceptor attaches the token to every request, and a guard blocks protected routes. This chapter wires them into one flow.
The service owns everything auth-related: calling the login API, storing the token (in localStorage so it survives refreshes), exposing it as a signal, and logging out.

blocks.label: auth.service.ts

blocks.text: A small form calls login(). On success it sends the user to where they were headed (the returnUrl), or to the dashboard.

blocks.label: login.ts

blocks.text: The guard (Chapter 32) blocks protected routes when logged out — and remembers where the user wanted to go by passing a returnUrl to the login page.

blocks.label: auth.guard.ts

blocks.text: The interceptor (Chapter 41) attaches the stored token to every request, and logs the user out on a 401.

blocks.label: auth.interceptor.ts

blocks.text: Register the interceptor, and protect routes with the guard.

blocks.label: app.routes.ts

blocks.text: Now: visiting /dashboard logged out → guard sends you to /login?returnUrl=/dashboard → after login you're sent back, and every API call carries your token.

items: AuthService logs in, stores the token (localStorage + signal), and logs out.
The login page redirects to returnUrl on success.
The guard blocks protected routes and passes a returnUrl.
The interceptor attaches the token and handles 401s.
Together they form a complete, real-world auth flow.
